feedback: No earlier iteration exists, so this feedback rests only on what the geometry implies and what the controller had to handle. The baseline 12 mm footprints at 10 mm spacing overlap the 25 mm tape, so a centred line gives about 0.5 to 1.0 signal on the inner sensors. Outer sensors can saturate when the line sits near the array edge, which is why I used a weight scale of ±2 and kp 2.0 rather than larger gains. The 4 cm forward offset means the controller reads the line before the wheels reach it, which required a derivative term (kd 0.15) to stop the lookahead from overshooting on bends. Once the race is run, use these rules: if line_loss_events is above zero or max_error exceeds 0.04 m on the slalom, widen the outer sensors (for example, x = ±0.03) so the tape stays under a sensor at the edge of the 0.06 m off-track limit. If steering_oscillation is high while rms_error is low, reduce the forward offset toward y = 0.02 so the controller reacts to the line later and less aggressively. If the robot completes with rms_error well under 0.02 m, try a narrower sensor_size of 0.008 to sharpen the signal across the tape.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events > 0 on the slalom: widen the outer sensors to x = -0.03 and x = +0.03, keeping the other three at the current spacing, so the array covers more of the 25 mm tape before the robot leaves the line. Evidence basis: the 0.06 m off-track limit and the 12 mm footprint leave the outer sensors near the edge on bends.

If steering_oscillation is high while rms_error is low: move the sensor row to y = 0.02 instead of 0.04, so the controller reads the line closer to the axle and reacts less aggressively. Evidence basis: the 4 cm lookahead required kd 0.15 in the baseline design to remain damped.

If the run completes with rms_error below 0.02 m and no line loss: set sensor_size to 0.008 to sharpen the reading across the tape, keeping the geometry otherwise unchanged. Evidence basis: the baseline 12 mm footprints overlap the 25 mm tape, which blurs the signal at small offsets.
